chapter: Then versus now, dances and carnival balls
title: Halls for the balls and the Gypsy Tea Room, Santa Simons Club
summary: They played Santa Simons, St. Catherine and the Gypsy Tea Room; he explains why new clubs book out-of-town bands.

blocks.x: Which halls did you use? Did you play? Those were carnival balls mostly. Did they have their own club rooms?

No. We played the Santa Simons Hall. We played St. Catherine Hall, carnival ball. We played the old Saint Sue Hall. You might have heard of that. Oh, yeah. I guess they tore that down. They tore that down. We played a lot of balls there. And they played most of them at the Santa Simons Club and St. Catherine. And played a few at the Gypsy Tea Room. Yeah. You might have heard of the Gypsy Tea Room.
Yeah. They call that tip top for a bar. They call it the hi-hat.
The hi-hat. Then they renamed it again to the Eptide. Oh, is it Eptide now?
Yeah. We played a lot of balls there. Most of the balls we played at this old Santa Simons Club. They renamed it now.
What would you down come? They still use that for dancing now? I haven't noticed any signs out in front. I think they took the big dancing sign down.

Which club is that? The Santa Simons Club. Yeah, they still use it. They name it the 5-4 Club. 5-4 Club. And they reopened it Sunday night. Oh, really? Oh, they just reopened it. Yeah, they reopened it Sunday night.
I thought somebody told me they were having dancing there now again, but I didn't know.
They reopened it Sunday night with an out-of-town band and an out-of-town singer.

Eta James. Yeah, Sunday night. Yeah. Why do you use an out-of-town? Well, to draw the people. Yeah, see? Is that right? See, when they open a new club like that, they use out-of-town attractions to draw the public. And after the people get to knowing it, well, they're using the local outfit.
Suppose the people think the out-of-town band's going to be better than the ones here?
No, it's not the question of it's better, but it's the question of you're not seeing them. Yeah, something new.
